question.problem:
Which of the following gives the area bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\sqrt{3}
$$

and the $x$-axis for $t\in [\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{2\pi }{3}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t) \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{2\pi /3}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\sqrt{3})(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-3{\int }_{\pi /3}^{2\pi /3}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\sqrt{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a negative number since $y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\le 0$ for all $t\in [\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{2\pi }{3}].$

Therefore, the area is given by

$$
A=-(-3{\int }_{\pi /3}^{2\pi /3}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\sqrt{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t)=3{\int }_{\pi /3}^{2\pi /3}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\sqrt{3})\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t.
$$
